title: Sequencing modules and how they relate
description: Connect sequencing and optical barcode workflows to phenotype scores, regression, experiment planning, power estimates, dose-response analysis and run comparison.
objectives: Choose a starting module from the data you already have.
Identify what each module reads and writes.
Follow the linked module lessons and API contracts for the next step.
prerequisite: Install spaCR and open Home. This lesson explains navigation and data handoffs; the linked module lessons provide the worked data examples. Inputs and outputs include conditional alternatives, as explained for each module.

scenes.narration: Start on Home with the question and the type of barcode data. Map Barcodes reads sequencing files; optical pooled screening reads registered image cycles through OPS. Both need an explicit mapping from barcode identities to the experiment. Regression relates compatible perturbation counts and phenotype scores; it does not replace barcode decoding. Experiment Design and Power belong before acquisition when you are planning the screen, while Dose-Response and Run Compare inspect suitable results afterwards.

Open Map Barcodes from Home. Supply the references that encode your experiment. Inspect mapped counts and barcode QC before pairing well-level guide counts with phenotype scores. Input data: Sequencing reads. Output data: Guide counts per well. Map Barcodes to Regression: Pair guide counts with phenotype scores using consistent plate/well keys. Map Barcodes to Barcode QC: Check mapping and coverage before guide filtering.

Open Map Barcodes from Home, then choose Barcode QC. Inspect mapping depth, coverage, collisions and positional effects before guide-count filtering. Input data: Guide counts per well. Output data: Quality-control results; Figures and table exports. Map Barcodes to Barcode QC: Check mapping and coverage before guide filtering.

Open Mask from Home, then choose OPS. Use sequencing-cycle images and phenotype alignment to decode barcodes per nucleus. Aggregate/join the decoded identities to compatible phenotype inputs before Regression; the OPS database is not a drop-in FASTQ count CSV. Input data: Microscope images; Aligned mosaic and coordinates. Output data: Optical barcode assignments. OPS to Regression: Join/aggregate decoded objects to phenotype and guide inputs explicitly before Regression; this is not a direct CSV handoff.

Open Regression from Home. Match plate and well identifiers across phenotype and guide-count inputs, select the response and controls, and inspect diagnostics before interpreting hits. Direct measured responses are also supported. Input data: Object classification scores; Guide counts per well; Optical barcode assignments; Measured objects. Output data: Regression results and hits. Classify to Regression: Select the intended CV or ML score column and preserve plate/well identity. Map Barcodes to Regression: Pair guide counts with phenotype scores using consistent plate/well keys. OPS to Regression: Join/aggregate decoded objects to phenotype and guide inputs explicitly before Regression; this is not a direct CSV handoff. Regression to Run Compare: Compare compatible saved result sets and their settings.

Open Power / Design from Home. Estimate sampling needs from chosen effect sizes and variability; pilot measurements are optional evidence for assumptions. Input data: Screen design and power estimates; Measured objects; Experimental layout. Output data: Screen design and power estimates. Experiment Design to Power / Design: Use the experimental layout to define sampling assumptions, then revise the design. Power / Design to Pooled-screen simulation sweep: Translate planning assumptions into the simulation settings dictionary manually; Power / Design does not export a ready-to-run simulation grid.

Open Experiment Design from Home. Enter conditions, controls, replicates and plate constraints, then export the experimental layout before acquisition. Input data: Screen design and power estimates. Output data: Experimental layout. Experiment Design to Power / Design: Use the experimental layout to define sampling assumptions, then revise the design. Experiment Design to Dose–Response: Acquire and measure the experiment first, preserving dose/condition identities. Pooled-screen simulation sweep to Experiment Design: Use simulated performance to reconsider sampling and plate constraints manually; the simulation database is not an importable plate layout.

Open Dose–Response from Home. Supply dose and response columns, controls and units before curve fitting; this route does not require sequencing. Input data: Measured objects; Experimental layout. Output data: Assay results; Figures and table exports. Experiment Design to Dose–Response: Acquire and measure the experiment first, preserving dose/condition identities.

Open Run Compare from Home. Compare compatible saved settings, counts and hit lists without treating changed input data as a controlled model comparison. Input data: Run history and artifacts; Regression results and hits. Output data: Run/model comparison. Regression to Run Compare: Compare compatible saved result sets and their settings.

Use Pooled-screen simulation sweep from Python through spacr.sim.run_multiple_simulations. This API-only workflow has no Home tile or menu entry. Use the Python sweep API to explore stated screen-design assumptions. It expands combinations, runs simulations in a process pool and writes synthetic summary statistics; it returns None. Set a small explicit max_workers value and a bounded parameter grid before running. The output does not replace measurements or barcode counts for experimental Regression. Use the findings as planning evidence, with their assumptions recorded. Input data: Pooled-screen simulation assumptions. Output data: Synthetic screen simulation summaries. Power / Design to Pooled-screen simulation sweep: Translate planning assumptions into the simulation settings dictionary manually; Power / Design does not export a ready-to-run simulation grid. Pooled-screen simulation sweep to Experiment Design: Use simulated performance to reconsider sampling and plate constraints manually; the simulation database is not an importable plate layout.

Keep sequencing references and plate layouts with the counts, and check the join to image-derived scores before interpreting a regression. Optical assignments require their own object join and aggregation; they are not automatically a drop-in sequencing count file. Treat planning assumptions, fitted effects and comparisons between completed runs as distinct results. The linked lessons and Home walkthroughs show the route for each kind of experiment.
